title: Coordinate-tower counits normalize section deformation charts
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\geq1$ with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be Noetherian with $N$ invertible on $S$. Work in the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse images. For every compactifiable structural map $b$ write $\omega_b=b^\times A$ using the right adjoint of $Rb_!$. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes d}$, with $A_T(0)=A_T$.
Fix $d\geq0$, let $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ have zero section $0$, and let $p_{d,X}:\mathbf A^d_X\to X$ for $X=\mathbf A^1_S$, $a:X\to S$. Identify the deformation of $(p_d,0)$ with $(p_{d,X},0_X)$ by $x_j=t u_j$. For either affine projection $p$ let $t_p:Rp_!A(d)[2d]\to A$ be the Kummer-normalized ordered coordinate-tower counit (the identity adjunction in dimension zero), and let $\alpha_p:A(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ be its adjoint under $Rp_!\dashv p^\times$. Then for every Noetherian base change $v:T\to S$ its actual counit-defined exceptional comparison $\beta$ satisfies
$$\beta\circ v_{\mathbf A^d}^*\alpha_{p_d}=\alpha_{p_{d,T}}$$
under the canonical Tate pullback identification. In particular, identifying $C=0^*\omega_{p_d}$ and $F=0_X^*\omega_{p_{d,X}}$ with the two Tate lines by these $\alpha$ maps, the section comparison $\theta:i_1^*F\to C$ is the identity. The comparison $F\to a^*C$ induced by the two orientations therefore has $i_1^*\lambda=\theta$.
More generally, let $g:V\to S$ be smooth separated compactifiable of dimension $d$, with closed section $s$, and let $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_T$ over an affine open $T\subseteq S$ be a separated etale coordinate neighbourhood of $s(T)$, carrying it to zero with Cartesian square of centres. Its induced Rees map has coordinates $x_j=t u_j$. Use the locality isomorphisms for compact-support right adjoints and the same $\alpha$ maps to form $\lambda:F|_{\mathbf A^1_T}\to a_T^*(C|_T)$, where $F$ is the section pullback of the Rees-family dualizing object and $C=s^*\omega_g$. Assume the Rees family and its chart composites are Noetherian, smooth where required, and compactifiable. Then $i_1^*\lambda=\theta|_T$ for the actual exceptional fibre map. Equivalently the correction $h=(i_1^*\lambda)\theta^{-1}$ is the identity.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [prop-asd-smooth-base-change].

proof.text: Put $L_p=A_{\mathbf A^d_S}(d)[2d]$. Use the explicit ordered tower adjunction in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], whose right functor is $p^*(-)(d)[2d]$. The unbounded composition comparisons of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identify its left functor with the actual $Rp_!$; on $L_p$ this identification agrees with the bounded-below one used to define $t_p$. Thus this is an adjunction on the same ordinary categories as $Rp_!\dashv p^\times$, not merely a calculation of one compact-support group. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], the counit-compatible comparison between their right adjoints is an isomorphism. At $A_S$ it is exactly $\alpha_p$, because its transpose is the specified $t_p$. In particular $\varepsilon_p\circ Rp_!(\alpha_p)=t_p$. This argument also applies over every Noetherian base under consideration, including $X=\mathbf A^1_S$.

source.place: Local construction, affine-space adjunction and the two identifications; counit-compatible choice of those identifications

proof.text:
For $v:T\to S$ write $v':\mathbf A^d_T\to\mathbf A^d_S$, $p'=p_{d,T}$, and $C_K:v^*Rp_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_!v'^*K$. Its normalization on $L_p$ is the exchange in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Let $\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_{p'}$ denote the exceptional counits at the constant object. The counit-defined $\beta$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] satisfies
$$\varepsilon_{p'}\circ Rp'_!(\beta)=v^*\varepsilon_p\circ C_{\omega_p}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $C$ and Step 1 therefore give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{p'}\circ Rp'_!(\beta\circ v'^*\alpha_p)
&=v^*\varepsilon_p\circ C_{\omega_p}^{-1}\circ Rp'_!(v'^*\alpha_p)\\
&=v^*(\varepsilon_p\circ Rp_!\alpha_p)\circ C_{L_p}^{-1}\\
&=v^*t_p\circ C_{L_p}^{-1}=t_{p'}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is precisely the arbitrary-Noetherian-base-change equality in the affine-space trace node. The adjunct of $\alpha_{p'}$ is also $t_{p'}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $\beta\circ v'^*\alpha_p=\alpha_{p'}$, with the canonical Tate identification of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Only the input $L_p$ in the trace calculation is bounded below; the exceptional adjunction and exchange remain the unbounded ones.

source.place: Local construction, standard affine model: explicit transposition of the normalized affine-space trace

proof.text:
In the standard deformation identification of the statement, $q=p_{d,X}$ and the section is $0_X$; at $t=1$, $x_j=u_j$, so its fibre chart is the original ordered coordinate chart. Write $B_S=A_S(d)[2d]$, $B_X=a^*B_S$, $o_C=0^*\alpha_{p_d}:B_S\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ and $o_F=0_X^*\alpha_q:B_X\xrightarrow{\sim}F$. Apply Step 2 over the Noetherian base $X$ to $i_1:S\to X$ and restrict to the zero section. The actual section exceptional comparison is exactly this restriction, giving $\theta\circ i_1^*o_F=o_C$. Consequently, for $\lambda_0=a^*o_C\circ o_F^{-1}$,
$$i_1^*\lambda_0=o_C\circ(i_1^*o_F)^{-1}=\theta.$$
Thus $\theta$ is the identity when its source and target are written in these Tate coordinates. The Tate identifications commute with the two section pullbacks by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The same calculation at $d=0$ uses the literal identity tower adjunction.

source.place: Local construction, standard model and its fibre at t=1

proof.text: Now work over the indicated affine open $T$ and put $X_T=\mathbf A^1_T$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow V_T$ be the coordinate neighbourhood and let $D_U$ be the deformation of its section. The Cartesian-centre condition and [lem-trf-section-rees-base-change-etale] give two section-preserving etale family maps: $D_U\to D_{s_T}V_T$ induced by $j$, and $D_U\to\mathbf A^d_{X_T}$ induced by $e$. Their maps at one are $j$ and $e$, respectively. On the coordinate algebra the latter is $x_j\mapsto t u_j$ and at one is $x_j\mapsto u_j$; hence it uses precisely the ordered fibre chart used for the source orientation. No invertibility of $t$ is used. The open inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. All structural maps and chart composites here have the Noetherian, smoothness and compactifiability hypotheses imposed in the item. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $V_T$ is Noetherian because its structural map is compactifiable and hence finite type; its open $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The separated etale chart maps are finite type: they are locally of finite type, and each inverse image of an affine target open is an open of a Noetherian source, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus the finite-type hypothesis in the two locality/coherence applications below is satisfied.

source.place: Local construction, Cartesian centres, induced etale Rees map, and x_j=t u_j

proof.text:
Write $F_0,C_0,\theta_0$ for the standard affine-space family over $T$; write $F_U,C_U,\theta_U$ for the chart family, and $F_T,C_T,\theta_T$ for the given family restricted to $T$. The counit-normalized locality isomorphisms of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], restricted to the sections, are
$$b_F^e:F_0\xrightarrow{\sim}F_U,\quad b_C^e:C_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C_U,\quad b_F^j:F_T\xrightarrow{\sim}F_U,\quad b_C^j:C_T\xrightarrow{\sim}C_U.$$
Apply the etale-family clause of [lem-trf-section-exceptional-fibre-coherence] to each of the two maps in Step 4. It states exactly
$$\theta_U\circ i_1^*b_F^e=b_C^e\circ\theta_0,\qquad
\theta_U\circ i_1^*b_F^j=b_C^j\circ\theta_T.$$
Here $\theta_T$ is the actual exceptional fibre map: the same node's base-change clause identifies its formation over $T$ with the restriction of $\theta$ over $S$. This uses the coherence of the specified counits, not a choice of abstract fibre isomorphisms. No assertion about the unique normalized global deformation isomorphism is needed from that node.

source.place: Step 3, ingredients pulled back: compatibility of the counit-normalized locality maps with the fibre map

proof.text:
The two chart orientations in the item give the following explicit uncorrected comparison, where $\lambda_0$ is Step 3 over $T$:
$$\lambda_U=a_T^*b_C^e\circ\lambda_0\circ(b_F^e)^{-1},\qquad
\lambda=(a_T^*b_C^j)^{-1}\circ\lambda_U\circ b_F^j.$$
Using Step 3 and the first equality in Step 5 yields
$$i_1^*\lambda_U=b_C^e\circ\theta_0\circ(i_1^*b_F^e)^{-1}=\theta_U.$$
The second equality in Step 5 then gives
$$i_1^*\lambda=(b_C^j)^{-1}\circ\theta_U\circ i_1^*b_F^j=\theta_T=\theta|_T.$$
All inverses exist by the cited locality isomorphisms. Therefore $h=(i_1^*\lambda)\circ(\theta|_T)^{-1}=1_{C_T}$. The calculation proves the claimed normalization for the orientations themselves; it neither presupposes that correction nor uses an independently chosen identification at one.
